name: VPN-Poppy
description: A personal VPN on the fly in your own AWS — one-click WireGuard endpoints on a t4g.nano, no SSH, QR/.conf for unlimited devices, live cost meter, teardown whenever or after N hours you set.

permissionSet.name: VPN-Poppy backend
permissionSet.description: Launch and manage a single EC2 endpoint it creates, scoped to its own tagged resources. Reads/creates on EC2; every change or delete is limited to instances and security groups tagged as its own. Reads CloudWatch metrics for the cost meter. No IAM, no key pairs, no account/org access.

grants.reason: Looks at the networks, system images and firewall settings already in your account, to offer you real choices when you set a VPN up — and checks on the servers it runs. It can look, never touch: every change it makes is covered by other, tighter permissions.

compliance.dataHandled: WireGuard keys and endpoint configuration, created and stored only in your own AWS account. No traffic, connection logs or keys ever reach the developer.
